# Capture projection state when grid keyboard navigation fails

## Context

The retained failure in [the investigation receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19515#issuecomment-6085142673) contains both stale c12 and correct c3 selected in the DOM. It has no worker-side snapshot, so it cannot identify where the stale projection began. The root-cause and repair acceptance criteria remain on `#19515`; this leaf delivers only the missing failure evidence.

## The Problem

Temporary terminal probes passed without reproducing the intermittent failure. Repeating unchanged green stress runs cannot classify that historical occurrence. The existing keyboard-scroll regression should retain useful model and projection evidence when it next fails in CI.

## The Architectural Reality

`test/playwright/e2e/grid/KeyboardNavigationScroll.spec.mjs` uses the Engine-only fixture and reads the first selected DOM cell. `src/grid/View.mjs:135` exposes selection-model items through `selectedCells`; `src/worker/App.mjs:384` exposes read-only `getConfigs`. Row VDOM and adopted vnode have different representations. These reads are sequential observations across threads, not one atomic snapshot.

Design authority: not applicable — this adds diagnostic evidence, without changing the existing navigation contract.

## The Fix

Add a failure-only afterEach collector in the existing spec. Capture DOM first (all selected cells, target/selected rows, identifiers, scroll position), then worker-backed selectedCells, row VDOM/vnode projections, mounted columns and update flags. Use the existing Engine RPC; retain Engine-only selection. Bound read waiting to three seconds, preserve partial evidence on read failure, and never replace the original failure when collection or attachment fails.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback / edge case | Docs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| New `grid-selection-state` JSON attachment | This diagnostic leaf; existing failure evidence linked above | Unexpected test failure attaches DOM and subsequent worker state with observation times | Missing grid/instances recorded; rejected or stalled reads retain partial evidence; attachment failure warns; original failure preserved | Collector JSDoc explains non-atomic reads and limits | Real-browser stale-DOM and stalled-worker controls |
| Existing keyboard-scroll arm | `KeyboardNavigationScroll.spec.mjs` and original regression contract | Original key sequence, timing and assertions unchanged; passing runs collect nothing | No per-key waits, retries, or alternate selected-cell choice | Existing spec narrative retained | Diff comparison and clean focused run |

Decision Record impact: none. Agent OS structure-map: N/A; this is an existing Engine test, with no new module or runtime surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An unexpected failure attaches the DOM-first and worker projection evidence described above, sufficient to distinguish a deliberately stale DOM class from a correct model/VDOM/vnode selection.
- [ ] A stalled worker read is bounded to three seconds, preserves the DOM snapshot and original assertion failure, and records the diagnostic error.
- [ ] The clean existing regression passes without a diagnostic attachment; its input sequence and assertions remain unchanged and it stays eligible for Engine-only E2E runs.

## Out of Scope

Reproducing or repairing the underlying intermittent producer, changing engine code, weakening assertions, broadening the test fixture, or closing `#19515`.

## Avoided Traps

A synthetic stale DOM is a control for the collector, not a reproduction of the original defect. Green reruns do not retire the historical failure. An always-on probe or per-key RPC would alter timing; a Brain fixture would remove this spec from Engine-only selection.
